answer: At the nadir of a sybil attack, when malicious agents seem to be flooding the network, a novel defense mechanism emerges, one that requires attackers to expend significant resources to mimic the behavior of legitimate users over the horizon of multiple interactions. By analyzing the timber of their digital footprints, the network can identify and reject fake identities that fail to demonstrate a consistent work trail, effectively raising the cost of launching a successful sybil attack and protecting the integrity of the agent economy.
